title: Browser Extensions & Privacy Add-ons Security Checklist
metaDescription: Essential security checklist for privacy-focused browser extensions, ad blockers, and security add-ons. Protect your browsing with uBlock Origin and more.
intro: Browser extensions can enhance privacy but also create security risks. This checklist helps you choose, configure, and maintain privacy-focused extensions safely while avoiding malicious add-ons that could compromise your data.

items.task: Only install extensions from official browser stores
items.why: Official stores have security reviews and can remove malicious extensions quickly, reducing malware risk.
items.howTo: Use Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, or Edge Add-ons. Avoid downloading .crx or .xpi files from third-party sites unless absolutely necessary.

items.task: Review all requested permissions before installing
items.why: Extensions requesting excessive permissions may access sensitive data beyond their stated purpose.
items.howTo: Read the permissions list carefully. Ad blockers need site access, but a calculator shouldn't need to read browsing history. Reject extensions with suspicious permission requests.

items.task: Verify extension developer and user reviews
items.why: Established developers with good reputations are less likely to create malicious extensions.
items.howTo: Check developer history, read recent reviews, look for red flags like sudden permission changes or suspicious behavior reports. Prefer extensions with 1000+ users and 4+ star ratings.

items.task: Install core privacy extensions: uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger
items.why: These proven extensions block ads, trackers, and malicious content without compromising security.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin for ad/tracker blocking and Privacy Badger for additional tracker protection. Both are open-source and regularly updated.

items.why: Default settings may not provide maximum protection against ads, trackers, and malicious content.
items.howTo: Enable additional filter lists like 'Annoyances' and 'Privacy'. Turn on 'Block remote fonts' and 'Disable JavaScript' for sensitive browsing. Use medium or hard mode for advanced users.

items.task: Keep installed extensions to minimum necessary
items.why: Each extension increases attack surface and potential privacy risks. More extensions mean more data access points.
items.howTo: Regularly audit your extensions. Remove unused ones. Aim for 5-10 essential extensions maximum. Consider Incognito Browser which has built-in privacy features reducing extension needs.

items.task: Disable non-essential extensions in private browsing
items.why: Extensions can track activity even in incognito mode unless explicitly disabled.
items.howTo: Go to browser extension settings and uncheck 'Allow in incognito/private' for all extensions except essential privacy tools like uBlock Origin.

items.task: Enable automatic updates for all extensions
items.why: Updates patch security vulnerabilities and improve protection against new tracking methods.
items.howTo: In browser settings, ensure 'Update extensions automatically' is enabled. Manually check for updates monthly in extension management page.

items.task: Watch for suspicious extension behavior or changes
items.why: Extensions can be sold to malicious actors or updated with harmful code after installation.
items.howTo: Notice if extensions request new permissions, show unexpected ads, or slow browsing significantly. Remove any extension exhibiting suspicious behavior immediately.

items.task: Quarterly review of all extension permissions
items.why: Extensions may request additional permissions through updates, expanding their data access.
items.howTo: Every 3 months, check each extension's current permissions in browser settings. Remove any that gained unnecessary permissions or are no longer needed.

items.why: Losing custom filter lists and settings requires time-consuming reconfiguration and may reduce protection temporarily.
items.howTo: Use uBlock Origin's backup feature to export settings. Document custom filter rules. Consider browser sync but be aware of privacy trade-offs.

items.task: Regularly test ad blocker and privacy extension effectiveness
items.why: Extensions may become less effective over time as advertisers and trackers develop new techniques.
items.howTo: Monthly, visit sites like d3ward.github.io/toolz/adblock.html to test ad blocking effectiveness. Check for missed ads or trackers and adjust settings accordingly.
